turns.assessment: The simultaneous OTU_LOF events are accompanied by nearly identical ~68–70 ps DGD increases and BER degradation across many channels, while optical power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry remain unchanged. This strongly identifies a common fibre PMD/DGD event rather than loss, amplifier, WSS, line-card, or OTN-switch failure. The only specifically aerial candidate is the same physical S01–S12 cable section represented directionally as E5 and E20; the evidence does not distinguish which directional span record should receive the repair, so neither reaches the 80% commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: E5 is the 90.3 km aerial span on S01→S12. A persistent DGD rise explains the common ~69 ps DGD jumps, consequent BER increase, LOF, and service failures without power or OSNR changes.

E20 is the reverse-direction representation of the same 90.3 km aerial cable section on S12→S01. It fits the observed DGD-only impairment equally well, but the supplied observations do not resolve direction.
An aerial cable can undergo polarization transients, but the sustained LOF and measured DGD level shift make a transient SOP event much less likely than DGD_RISE.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
